title: Implicit type casts and zero dates break on PostgreSQL
summary: Seven call sites compare text with numbers, and 18,516 rows hold the zero date. Bind the parameters as strings and convert each zero date to NULL during the copy.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: MySQL converts types without a warning. PostgreSQL does not. Two patterns in the code and the data depend on the MySQL behaviour.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [READ] 7 call sites compare a VARCHAR column with a number. An example is WHERE order_number = ? with a long parameter. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] PostgreSQL rejects 5 of the 7 with operator does not exist: character varying = bigint. [src: report.md]
  • [UNVERIFIED] The staging tests do not reach the other 2 call sites. I expect the same error.
  • [TESTED] 18,204 rows in orders.shipped_at and 312 rows in returns.closed_at hold 0000-00-00 00:00:00. PostgreSQL does not accept this value. [src: report.md]
  • [READ] The service already reads the zero date as NULL (zeroDateTimeBehavior=convertToNull). [src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html: A failed comparison returns an error page to the customer. A zero date stops the bulk copy of its table.

blocks.title: Proposed action
blocks.html:
1. Bind the 7 parameters as strings.
  2. Add a test for each of the 7 call sites.
  3. Set the copy tool to write NULL for each zero date.

Effort: 1.5 days. The service already reads the zero date as NULL, so its behaviour does not change.
